### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **17** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/src/security/permission.zod.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**18** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0d1443d0bf7560a6be9a1a7be8012db26159baa4`.

⛔ **7** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/src/security/permission.zod.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **5** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **184** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0d1443d0bf7560a6be9a1a7be8012db26159baa4` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `fafe3bf9f2b4090ce8d8d07ca24bce6058fba288` — the merge of head `25dcfa863613d10673918f081c89e6d0b09b558d` into base `0d1443d0bf7560a6be9a1a7be8012db26159baa4`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin fafe3bf9f2b4090ce8d8d07ca24bce6058fba288 && git checkout fafe3bf9f2b4090ce8d8d07ca24bce6058fba288
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 0d1443d0bf7560a6be9a1a7be8012db26159baa4 25dcfa863613d10673918f081c89e6d0b09b558d && git checkout -B drift-repro 0d1443d0bf7560a6be9a1a7be8012db26159baa4 && git merge --no-ff 25dcfa863613d10673918f081c89e6d0b09b558d

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0d1443d0bf7560a6be9a1a7be8012db26159baa4
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 0d1443d0bf7560a6be9a1a7be8012db26159baa4` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `0245cb6d7bc4969fd9f6f1551ef000e399970c0d`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/security/permission.zod.ts, docs/adr/0066-unified-authorization-model.md + .changeset/33828-own-field-mask-binds-over-own-view-all.md, packages/core/src/security/effective-object-permissions.ts, packages/core/src/security/superuser-field-vote-33828.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/permission-evaluator.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/fls-own-field-mask-33828.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/explain-principal-person.test.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-security-posture.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-security-posture.user-text.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-security-posture.test.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-security-posture-own-field-mask-33828.test.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-rollup-source-visibility.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-rollup-source-visibility.test.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-rollup-source-visibility-own-field-mask-33828.test.ts, packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts, packages/lint/src/finding-user-text.test.ts, content/docs/permissions/authorization.mdx, content/docs/permissions/permissions-matrix.mdx

Read at 2026-11-15T20:18Z. First review of this head, taken on patrol as owed; claim: comment 6900513648. Independence: implemented in a zhuangjianguo lane (domain:server#5); neither dispatched nor implemented by os-tesla.

Read: the whole diff against merge base `b8ac0e240`, the PR body and thread, the card and its thread, the head's check-runs and the log of the one red job. Read outside the diff, never reviewed: the callers of the field merge in plugin-security, the consumers of the readable-field answer in the other packages, the shipped default permission sets, `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs`, `scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs`, the stock changesets `4138ce8` and `33689-ai-action-confirmation-elicited.md`.

### ① Derived judgments

- **The rule.** ADR-0066 D2 ⑧, note of 2026-11-15: a set that holds View All on an object, and not Modify All, casts no read vote on a field its own row declares `readable: false`. The tree keeps it. One function answers the per-field vote and both field merges ask it with the field's name. The note quotes the card's ruling word for word.
- **Same set only.** The mask is read on the set that declares it and never on a sibling. Another set's View All, Modify All or declared `readable: true` still reads the field, in either resolution order. No holder of another set alone loses a field. Pinned from both sides in core and plugin-security, with the shipped `admin_full_access` as one of the second sets.
- **Not wider than declared.** A View All set still votes on every field it does not mask itself. Modify All votes as before, its own rows included, also when both bits sit on one entry. An omitted `readable` is not a mask. An edit lock beside View All binds as before. The row-level bypass does not read the field rows.
- **One case worth saying aloud.** A holder of the masked View All set plus a plain set that grants the object and names no field loses the field, although the plain set alone would serve it. That is the standing rule of the merge (only a vote reads a field a held set masks), it is pinned, and the holder holds the declaring set, so it is inside the declared narrowing. The changeset's phrase "a caller whom no other set serves the field to" is true only when "serves" is read as "votes"; see N1.
- **Doors.** Every reader of field permissions I traced takes its answer from the one merge: the result mask, the filter and sort guard, the field-level write gate, the readable-field answer the schema, reference-name, approvals, audit, analytics and storage readers ask, the access explanation, and the `fields` slot of `/auth/me/permissions`. I found no reader that decides a field from the View All bit ahead of the merge. Whether every transport applies field security at all is not moved by this diff and was not audited end to end here.
- **Shipped sets.** The default sets that withhold identity fields hold no View All or Modify All, and the admin sets carry keeping rows. The PR's statement that no shipped set carries the pair holds on the tree.
- **Lint.** `security-superuser-field-mask-inert` now gates on the set's own Modify All and is silent beside View All alone, through the object entry, the wildcard and a wildcard Modify All shadowed by an explicit View All entry. `security-controlled-by-parent-master-reference-hidden` speaks beside View All, which is right now that the mask binds there. The roll-up source rules read a View All set's own mask as hiding the field on parent and child. Each new finding is a true one under the new rule; I found no new false positive on a valid stack. Rule ids unchanged. The card's three hotcrm rows stop being reported.
- **Schema face.** `permission.zod.ts` changes a doc comment only. No shape, description or generated artifact moves, and the repo gates for generated files are green on this head. The published description of `when` speaks of a co-held set that says nothing about the field and stays true.
- **Tests.** 40 new pins, all on the two merges and the lint rules, each with a control or reverse pin and with multi-set cases in both orders. None goes through a booted data door; see S4.
- **Card acceptance.** Met for View All: both merges, the second-set Modify All reverse pin, the ADR amendment, the lint change. The card's Modify All half is left undecided; see S3.

### ② Semver level

- Declared: `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, `patch` on core, plugin-security, lint and spec, `!` in the title, a BREAKING paragraph, `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)`. The carrier, the "who moves" paragraph and the one-line remedy are present. A FROM/TO block is not owed, since no authorable key is removed or renamed.
- M1 (must-fix) — the kind is `semantic`, not `none`, so the level is wrong. AGENTS.md: "a changed meaning or default is `semantic`", and a kind takes at least `minor`. What an author already writes (a `readable: false` row in a set that holds View All on the object) changes meaning for that set's holders: from binding none of them to hiding the field. The ADR note itself says it replaces the sentence that told authors the row withholds nothing, and the two docs pages change their advice to authors. The stock changeset `33689-ai-action-confirmation-elicited.md` declares `semantic` for the same kind of move (an authorable key whose runtime meaning changes). The precedent the PR cites, `4138ce8`, declared `none` for the mirror change, and the PR body puts the question to the reviewer; this is the answer. Remedy: declare `Metadata-protocol: semantic` in the PR body and the changeset and grade the level the gate then asks for, or bring a ruling of record that `none` governs runtime-merge changes of this kind.
- S1 (should-fix) — the ADR-0087 disposition rests on "nothing for a migration to rewrite", while the same body tells an administrator which stored row to delete to keep the old answer. That is a judgment only the author can make on stored metadata, which is what a semantic entry under `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/` carries to the upgrade guide (compare `permission-write-without-read-refused`). Register one, or say in the marker why the upgrade guide need not name the pair.
- S2 (should-fix) — `superuserFieldVote` is exported from `@objectstack/core`, and it gains an optional third parameter and an accepted `fields` member on its input. That widens a public surface, so by the stock reading ("yes (narrowing) … the one widening is …") the value is `yes (narrowing)` with the widening named.
- **CI on this head: not green.** 68 check-runs: 56 success, 10 skipped, 2 failure. The failures are `Test Core (7/8)` and its roll-up `Test Core`: `@objectstack/scenarios`, `test/runner/run-date.test.ts`, three cases, each "Test timed out in 5000ms". The diff touches no scenarios file and the suites of the four touched packages are green in their shards. It still has to be green before anything lands. No check is in progress.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `docs/adr/**` is a Tier H governed surface: the note lands only on the maintainer's word, whatever this record says. No agent seat approves, queues or arms it.
- `packages/spec` is touched by a comment only; no baseline or generated doc is owed.
- `@objectstack/lint`: the finding's `userTextParams` lose `bypass`. No reader of that key exists in this repo outside the rule's own catalog.
- Consumer: hotcrm#2481 waits on a release that carries this.
- Base: the head was measured on `b8ac0e240`; `main` has moved, with one unrelated hunk in `rule-explanations.ts`. CI ran on the merge with `d3bea96d8`.
- Security discipline: this record stays at the rule level. Mechanism-level notes for the seat are in `scratchpad/pr-34082/security-notes.md`, not on the thread.

### ④ Design judgment

- `docs/adr/0066-unified-authorization-model.md` — holds against the code it cites (`superuserFieldVote`, both merges, the lint rule) and against its first consumer, the card's `project_member` rows. It amends the 2026-11-02 sentence for View All only and says so. It leaves a ruling pending with no carrier; S3.
- `packages/spec/src/security/permission.zod.ts` — the comment agrees with the merge. Nit N2.
- `effective-object-permissions.ts`, `permission-evaluator.ts` — agree with the note. The narrowing makes a declared mask real for the declaring set's holders and takes nothing from anyone else.
- `validate-security-posture.ts`, its user text, `rule-explanations.ts`, `validate-rollup-source-visibility.ts` — agree with the runtime rule, set by set.
- Against the published spec on `main`: the spec says `readable: false` hides a field; before this diff a set's own View All made that false for its holders. The narrowing makes the spec's own statement real. It does take a field away from holders who read it until now, which is why M1 and S1 matter.

Findings:

- M1 (must-fix) — `Metadata-protocol: none` should be `semantic`, and the level follows the kind (②).
- S1 (should-fix) — ADR-0087: register a semantic entry for the pair, or justify its absence against the body's own remedy (②).
- S2 (should-fix) — `Clause-②` value: the exported `superuserFieldVote` signature widens (②).
- S3 (should-fix) — `Fixes #33828` closes the card while its Modify All half ("or `editable: false`", "View All / Modify All") is left "pending a ruling" in the ADR. Name the card that carries that ruling in the PR body, or do not close this one.
- S4 (should-fix) — no pin goes through a booted door, and the dogfood battery the narrowing arm owes on the final head has no reading on the card. Post that reading before landing; one door-level pin for a holder of the pair (a list read and `/auth/me/permissions`) with the second-set control would hold the rule where consumers meet it.
- N1 (nit) — changeset and `authorization.mdx`: "serves the field to" and "reads the field" mean "casts a read vote on it"; a plain co-held set that names no field does not restore it. One clause would say so.
- N2 (nit) — `content/docs/permissions/field-level-security.mdx` (not in the diff) still tells the reader a mask holds unless another set unmasks it, without the own-set Modify All case; worth a line when the Modify All ruling lands.

### ① Derived judgments

- **What moved since `0245cb6d`.** One merge of `main` and one fix commit. The PR's own change measured before the merge (against `b8ac0e240`) and after it (against `86350e125`) is the same patch, the same 19 files. The head adds only `25dcfa86`: the changeset, `authorization.mdx`, one new semantic entry and one new dogfood test, for 21 files. No source of core, plugin-security or lint changed in this round, so the judgments of 6900701652 on the rule, the two merges, the doors and the lint rules stand unchanged.
- **The merge of `main`.** Of the PR's files, `main` touched only `rule-explanations.ts`, in an unrelated entry; the PR's hunk there is unchanged. Near the evaluation, `main` brought the View All parent-chain change (#33897, ruling #33696) and the bare doc read (#34036). The first is a row-level rule that reads the object-level bits and never the field merge; the second is metadata addressing. Neither changes an answer of the field-permission merge, and the first agrees with the PR's statement that the row-level bypass does not read field rows. `main` has moved further since (to `0d1443d0b`), with no commit on a file of this diff; CI ran on that merge.
- **Prior M1 (kind and level): closed.** The PR body and the changeset declare `Metadata-protocol: semantic`. The changeset grades core and plugin-security `minor`, lint and spec `patch`. The level gate reads it as semantic with a package at `minor` and is green.
- **Prior S1 (ADR-0087): closed.** The marker is `registered permission-own-field-mask-binds-over-own-view-all`, and the entry exists under `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/`. It names the surface, tells an administrator how to find the pair and what to decide in either direction, and says why no mechanical rewrite exists. Its statements agree with the code: Modify All excluded, the wildcard included, an omitted `readable` is not a mask, the co-held-set case. Its claim that the lint warning lists the pair on releases from 18.3.0 agrees with the lint changelog.
- **Prior S2 (`Clause-②`): closed.** The value is `yes (narrowing)` on the body, the changeset and claim amendment 2, and the changeset names the one widening (the optional third argument of `superuserFieldVote`, with the two-argument answer unchanged).
- **Prior S3 (closing keyword): closed.** The body says `Part of #33828` and that the Modify All half stays open on the card. No commit message on the branch carries a closing keyword. The card stays open as the carrier.
- **Prior S4 (door pin and battery): changed, half closed.** The door pin exists: on a booted showcase, a holder of the pair alone and a second member who also holds a plain View All set are each asked at `/auth/me/permissions` and at the list door, with a premise test and a guard against an empty list. That half is closed. The battery half is open: the card carries no dogfood reading for this head (its last comment is claim amendment 2), and the PR body says the battery is not measured on this head. See S1 below.
- **Prior N1 (wording): closed.** The changeset, `authorization.mdx` and the entry now say a holder reads the field only when another set casts a read vote on it, and that a co-held set that says nothing about the field does not restore it.
- **Prior N2 (`field-level-security.mdx`): open, unchanged.** Not in the diff. The body defers the line to the Modify All ruling, which is what the nit asked. Carried as N1 below.

### ② Semver level

- Declared: `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: semantic`, `minor` on core and plugin-security, `patch` on lint and spec, `!` in the title, a BREAKING paragraph, `adr-0087: registered permission-own-field-mask-binds-over-own-view-all`. The body, the changeset and claim amendment 2 agree line for line.
- The level is right. The meaning of a row an author already writes changes in the merge that core and plugin-security own, so those two take `minor`. Lint follows with a narrower finding and no change to an authorable key; spec gains a comment and an upgrade-guide entry. `patch` is acceptable for both.
- A FROM/TO block is carried by the entry's replacement text, as its siblings do.
- **CI on this head: green in effect.** 72 check-runs, all completed: 59 success, 12 skipped, 1 failure. The failure is a superseded `Check Changeset` run that read the PR body before it was edited (it still saw `no (narrowing)` and `none` beside the new `minor` grades). The run triggered by the body edit is green on the same head, as are `Test Core`, its shard 7 that was red on the previous head, the governed-surface guards and the PR-body guards. No check is in progress.
- One limit of that green: on a pull-request event CI does not run the dogfood package (its shards are skipped and `Test Core` excludes it). The new door pin therefore has no CI reading on this head; its reading is the author's local one in the PR body, and the queue build will be the first CI reading.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `docs/adr/**` is a Tier H governed surface: the note lands only on the maintainer's word, whatever this record says. No agent seat approves, queues or arms it. The ADR text did not change in this round.
- `packages/spec`: one new semantic entry and a comment. The registry and upgrade-guide gates are green on this head.

### ④ Design judgment

- `18.permission-own-field-mask-binds-over-own-view-all.ts` — holds against the rule the code implements and against the ruling it cites. It is the right kind of entry: both outcomes are access decisions, so it prescribes a judgment and no rewrite. Against its first consumer, the card's `project_member` rows, the instruction "keep the row" gives the outcome the card asked for.
- `docs/adr/0066-unified-authorization-model.md`, `packages/spec/src/security/permission.zod.ts` — unchanged since 6900701652; the judgment there stands. The pending Modify All ruling now has a carrier, the open card.

- The remaining implementing files are byte-identical to the head 6900701652 judged, and agree with the note.
- Against the published spec on `main`: the narrowing makes the spec's own statement, that `readable: false` hides a field, real for the declaring set's holders. It takes a field from holders who read it until now; that is now declared as `semantic`, graded, and carried to the upgrade guide.

The reading from `0245cb6d` does not carry over, because `main` came in between. Post the reading on the card before this is queued; the seat should not land on this record alone until it is there and green.
- N1 (nit) — continues prior N2. `content/docs/permissions/field-level-security.mdx` still lacks the own-set Modify All case; it goes with the Modify All ruling on the open card.
